+## #2862 - Hole-work catalog case
+
+**What was decided.** Add one original 90 x 90 x 20 mm plate with four
+drill holes on a 60 mm bolt circle. Use a separate hole for Bore, Circular
+and Thread. Add a tap-drill operation before the internal M8 x 1.25 thread.
+Use the existing command scripts, catalog discovery and default Fanuc mill
+post. Keep the model embedded in the saved project.
+
+**Why.** One small case makes the four operation types easy to compare.
+The posted program shows G81 cycles, hole milling arcs and the thread
+helix. The prior tap drill gives the thread mill an open hole. An embedded
+mesh lets the project open without a path relative to the script directory.
+The multi-form thread mill tip follows the helix from Z8 to Z9.875. Its
+axial cutting teeth cover the intended 12 mm thread length.
+
+**Model and tool choices.** The original generator tiles annular cells and
+checks their edge pairs. It uses 96 flats around each hole. The drill,
+bore and circular envelopes have 0.2 mm radial clearance. The thread hole
+keeps the M8 x 1.25 minor radius, 3.3235 mm, with its floor at Z4.
+The script extends the drill and end-mill flutes to 25 mm. A custom
+6.6 mm tap drill starts from the catalog drill. No holder is modelled.
+
+**What was dropped.** Do not use automatic drilling cycle selection.
+An explicit Drill cycle makes G81 stable when the hole dimensions change.
+Do not use a 10 mm radius Circular cut with several radial passes in this
+case. Verification refused that cut because of rapids through stock.
+Helical entry also produced crossing warnings. Use a 5 mm radius cut with
+a plunge entry; it needs one radial pass and verifies without warnings.
+The separate Circular defect is #2898. It is linked from #2862 and the
+catalog umbrella #2392.
+
+**Limits.** The through-drill point reaches Z-2.803 and the bore reaches
+Z-1. These moves require clearance below the plate. The report names the
+break-through. The case has no fixture or spoil board. No machine or
+control simulator has run the program. The model represents the thread
+minor hole, not its teeth.
+
+**Cost to change later.** A different hole size, tool, entry or cycle
+requires a script change and a rebuild of the committed project and NC
+program. A change to the model also requires a generator change. Update
+the case pin and README when their stated dimensions or output change.

+# Hole work
+
+This case shows Drill, Bore, Circular and Thread on an original
+90 x 90 x 20 mm plate. The plate has four drill holes on a 60 mm bolt
+circle. Two larger holes and one blind threaded hole show the other
+operations. All dimensions are in millimetres.
+
+| Operation | Tool | Position and cut |
+|---|---|---|
+| Bolt circle | DR-0600, diameter 6 | Four holes at (0, 30), (30, 0), (0, -30), (-30, 0) |
+| Bore | EM-0600-4FL, diameter 6 | Diameter 16 at (-30, 30), through the plate |
+| Circular | EM-0600-4FL, diameter 6 | Diameter 10 at (30, 30), down to Z0 |
+| Tap drill | TAP-DRILL, diameter 6.6 | Blind hole at (0, 0), point down to Z4 |
+| Thread | TM-0600-P125, diameter 6 | Right-hand internal M8 x 1.25 at (0, 0), Z8 to Z20 |
+
+The drill and end mill use 25 mm flutes. `TAP-DRILL` starts from the
+catalog drill and changes its diameter, shank diameter and flute length.
+The tools have no modelled holders.
+
+## What to inspect
+
+- `Bolt circle` posts four G81 cycles. `Tap drill` posts one more G81 cycle.
+- `Bore` posts arcs around (-30, 30) at successive depths.
+- `Circular` uses a plunge entry and arcs around (30, 30).
+- `Thread` posts G03 blocks with simultaneous XY and Z motion. The
+  multi-form thread mill cuts one helical turn for each radial pass.
+  Its tip moves between Z8 and Z9.875. Its axial cutting teeth cover
+  the intended 12 mm thread length; the helix does not rise to Z20.
+- The saved project embeds the mesh. It opens without a model source link.
+
+The generated mesh uses 96 flats around each hole. The drill, bore and
+circular holes have 0.2 mm of radial envelope clearance. The thread hole
+uses the M8 x 1.25 minor radius, 3.3235 mm. Its modelled floor is Z4.
+The model does not contain thread teeth.
+
+The Circular cut uses one radial pass. A larger cut with several radial
+passes exposed verification refusals tracked in #2898.
+
+The drill point reaches Z-2.803 on the bolt circle. The bore reaches Z-1
+because of its break-through setting. The verification report names these
+moves below the stock. No fixture or spoil board is modelled. Provide
+clearance below the plate before adapting this program to a machine.
+This case has not run on a machine or in a control simulator.
+
+## Rebuild
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+python3 examples/catalog/2d/hole-work/model/gen_hole_work_obj.py
+cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/hole-work
+cargo xtask catalog --check
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog
+```
+
+The generator checks that each mesh edge has one reverse edge. The build
+script creates the document through commands, generates all operations,
+requires a clean verification result, saves the project and posts the NC
+program with the default Fanuc mill post.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Provenance: original annular-cell plate mesh for CamCraft issue #2862."""
+from collections import Counter
+from math import cos, sin, tau
+from pathlib import Path
+
+N = 96
+TOP = 20.0
+# Four drill envelopes on a 60 mm bolt circle, a bore, a circular pocket,
+# and the M8x1.25 minor hole. The thread has a deeper tap-drill floor.
+HOLES = {(0, 30): (3.2, 0), (30, 0): (3.2, 0),
+         (0, -30): (3.2, 0), (-30, 0): (3.2, 0),
+         (-30, 30): (8.2, 0), (30, 30): (5.2, 0),
+         (0, 0): (3.3235, 4)}
+
+
+def build():
+    faces = []
+    for cx in (-30, 0, 30):
+        for cy in (-30, 0, 30):
+            radius, floor = HOLES.get((cx, cy), (0, 0))
+
+            def point(k, z, inner=False):
+                x, y = cos(tau * (k % N) / N), sin(tau * (k % N) / N)
+                scale = radius if inner else 15 / max(abs(x), abs(y))
+                return (round(cx + scale * x, 10), round(cy + scale * y, 10), z)
+
+            for k in range(N):
+                p, q = point(k, TOP), point(k + 1, TOP)
+                b, c = point(k, 0), point(k + 1, 0)
+                if radius:
+                    i, j = point(k, TOP, True), point(k + 1, TOP, True)
+                    u, v = point(k, floor, True), point(k + 1, floor, True)
+                    faces.extend([(p, q, j, i), (v, u, i, j)])
+                    if floor == 0:
+                        faces.append((c, b, u, v))
+                    else:
+                        faces.extend([((cx, cy, floor), u, v), ((cx, cy, 0), c, b)])
+                else:
+                    faces.extend([((cx, cy, TOP), p, q), ((cx, cy, 0), c, b)])
+                # Only the external plate boundary needs vertical walls.
+                if ((p[0] == q[0] and abs(p[0]) == 45)
+                        or (p[1] == q[1] and abs(p[1]) == 45)):
+                    faces.append((b, c, q, p))
+    return faces
+
+
+def main():
+    faces = build()
+    edges = Counter((p, q) for face in faces for p, q in zip(face, face[1:] + face[:1]))
+    for (p, q), count in edges.items():
+        if p == q or count != 1 or edges[(q, p)] != 1:
+            raise SystemExit(f"mesh has an open, repeated or degenerate edge: {p}, {q}")
+    vertices = dict.fromkeys(p for face in faces for p in face)
+    indices = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(vertices, 1)}
+    out = Path(__file__).with_name("hole-work.obj")
+    lines = ["# Original 90 x 90 x 20 mm hole-work plate; generated by gen_hole_work_obj.py."]
+    lines.extend("v %.10g %.10g %.10g" % p for p in vertices)
+    lines.extend("f " + " ".join(str(indices[p]) for p in face) for face in faces)
+    out.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+    print(f"wrote {out.name}: {len(vertices)} vertices, {len(faces)} faces")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
